title: What is ES6?
overview: ES6 (ECMAScript 2015) is a major update to JavaScript that introduced new features to make code cleaner, shorter, and easier to maintain.

example.title: ES6 Features
example.content:
Major ES6 features:
• let and const
• Arrow functions
• Template literals
• Destructuring
• Classes
• Modules

title: let and const
overview: ES6 introduced let and const for better variable declaration. They provide block scope and replace many use cases of var.

title: Arrow Functions
overview: Arrow functions provide a shorter syntax for writing functions and are commonly used in modern JavaScript and React Native development.

title: Template Literals
overview: Template literals allow developers to create strings using backticks and insert variables directly using interpolation.

title: Destructuring Assignment
overview: Destructuring allows extracting values from arrays and objects into separate variables using a simple syntax.

title: Spread Operator
overview: The spread operator allows copying or expanding elements from arrays and objects. It is widely used in React and React Native.

title: Rest Operator
overview: The rest operator collects multiple values into a single array or object. It is useful when handling dynamic data.

title: Classes in JavaScript
overview: ES6 introduced classes as a cleaner way to create objects and implement object-oriented programming concepts.

title: Modules Import and Export
overview: ES6 modules allow JavaScript code to be divided into multiple files using export and import statements.

example.title: Module Example
example.content:
export default App;

import App from './App';

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned important ES6 features including let, const, arrow functions, template literals, destructuring, spread, rest, classes, and modules.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ ES6 modernized JavaScript.
✔ let and const replaced var.
✔ Arrow functions simplify functions.
✔ Spread and rest handle data easily.
✔ Modules organize code.
